findings.title: Recreate exit code changed from 4 to 3 breaks the documented CLI contract
findings.body: This changes `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and assigns 4 to feature-disabled. The update compatibility docs explicitly tell users to script against the exit codes, so existing scripts that check for 4 to detect a required recreate upgrade will now classify recreate upgrades as feature-disabled and may choose the wrong upgrade strategy. If backward compatibility with the previously documented preview behavior matters, leave recreate at 4 and choose a separate code such as 5 for feature-disabled, or call out the break clearly.

findings.title: New CLI exit codes are not asserted
findings.body: `testWrongVersions` only asserts the stderr message and never checks `result.exitCode()`. The PR changes the recreate exit code to 3 and introduces feature-disabled exit code 4, but the tests would still pass if the command printed the expected error and returned the wrong exit code. Since the exit code is the primary scripting contract, assert exit code 3 for the wrong-version cases, exit code 4 for `testFeatureNotEnabled`, and exit code 0 for the successful check path.

findings.title: Caution overstates when the operator will fail without rolling-updates
findings.body: The new caution says the feature must be enabled, otherwise the Operator will fail. However, the default update strategy path (`spec.update` unset) uses legacy behavior and the operator tests in this PR do not enable the feature for that path: `createInitialDeployment(null)` returns before setting a `FeatureSpec`. The documentation should clarify that the feature is required when using the new `spec.update` strategy rather than stating that every Keycloak CR will fail without it.

findings.title: Example contains an invalid CRD value for update strategy
findings.body: The YAML example uses `strategy: Recreate|<not set>`, which is not a valid value for the update strategy field. A user copying this example would get a schema validation error. The listing should use `strategy: Recreate` for the example, with the unset/default behavior described separately in the callout or table.
